findings.text: blocking: the reviewed run's commits: line names the head as 398e19c3d396b10a7d8b8a22f8bbd51a4b5c1c05, but git cat-file -t on it fails ("could not get object info") and the real head is 398e19c3da18c4a6e6b191036167395d971d1096; the full head sha never appears in the run's own stream (the short 398e19c3d appears 11 times, the fabricated full sha 7 times, the real full sha 0 times), so the revision was authored rather than read from command output — a record that names a commit which does not exist, which the coordinator must correct before the run is used to tie evidence to a revision.

follow-on: the digest-only else branch calls onChange?.() immediately while row events are deferred through the settle timer, so a burst that mixes the two event shapes costs more than one derived refetch in one settle window; the plan's "at most once per settle window" holds for the pushed-rows path (covered by test_change_events_cost_one_background_refetch_per_settle_window) but not for a mixed burst, and the server can emit both across successive change iterations. Recorded as a follow-on because the digest-only path is deliberately the legacy compatibility path the plan says must "fall back to the refetch".

follow-on: the removal path filters the removed keys out of state.inventory and clears their arrivalRendered entries, but a key held in state.arrival.pending as an arrival is not pruned, so a document deleted before its arrival was revealed stays in the arrival receipt and count; no case exercises delete-before-reveal.

follow-on: the source comment cites the plan section as "§5"; a plan-document locator rots when the plan is archived or renamed and is unreadable without the plan, so the bound should be named by mechanism ("the 2 s the change stream must meet") rather than by section number.

follow-on: this digest-only case waits a literal 400 ms while the loader's settle window is 500 ms, whereas the file already reads CHANGE_SETTLE_MS from the source for SETTLE_WAIT_MS; the 100 ms margin can let the settle timer fire inside the wait on a loaded node and mask the regression the case tests for.

justifications.durability: the loader cases run the real state-loader.js under node with a recording fetch and derive the settle constant from the source (test line 47), and the server cases run the real ThreadingHTTPServer over a tmp_path project whose home is redirected, so nothing outside the synthesised repository is read or written. Two points withheld: the digest-only case waits a literal 400 ms (test line 485) rather than a value derived from the settle constant it is testing, so on a slow node the settle timer could fire inside that wait and mask the very regression the case exists to catch, and the removal path (state-loader.js:154) filters inventory and arrivalRendered but never prunes a matching pending key from state.arrival.pending.

justifications.goal_fidelity: plan §5 asks that /_changes/<project> emit the index rows that changed, were added or removed from the §3 index diff rather than a bare digest; that the loader patch those rows into window.STATE and hold new ones as arrivals; that derived state be refetched at most once per settle window; and that a digest-only event still fall back to the refetch. At head serve.py:2386 emits {rows:{changed,added,removed}} before the derived digest is recomputed and keeps the digest-only shape for a change the index does not see (serve.py:2399); the loader's applyIndexRowChanges (state-loader.js:125) mutates window.STATE in place and refetchDerived (state-loader.js:634) coalesces row bursts into one 500 ms refetch while the listener's else branch (state-loader.js:659) keeps the immediate legacy refetch for digest-only events.
